title: "12 Qualitative synthesis of methods research"
link-citations: true

Alternative labels: qualitative systematic reviews of methods research

## Definition and features
In qualitative syntheses of methods research, researchers synthesize findings, concepts, explanations, recommendations, or arguments from text-rich methodological research, such as interview studies or guidance documents. They usually start with a focused qualitative question, search for eligible publications using a comprehensive or purposeful sampling strategy, assess study quality, and use an explicit qualitative synthesis method, such as thematic synthesis.

- Strengths include transparency and comprehensiveness. 
- Key challenges are the difficult search and the lack of quality criteria for qualitative methods research.


::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Boundaries with related types

Boundary with A11 scoping review. Both use systematic searches and may include qualitative categorisation but scoping reviews do not typically include formal quality assessment or an interpretive synthesis of findings. The distinction can be difficult in practice, especially when a scoping review goes beyond description or when a qualitative synthesis mainly maps the literature.

**Similarities and differences between literature-based types:**

| Characteristic | [Review of applied methods](9review-applied.qmd) | [Meta-epidemiological study](10meta-epi.qmd) | [Scoping review of methods research](11scoping-review.qmd) | [Qualitative synthesis of methods research](12qualitative-synthesis.qmd) | [Quantitative synthesis of methods research](13quantitative-synthesis.qmd) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Typical purpose | Assess methodological practice or quality | Assess impact of methodological characteristics on study results | Identify available methods or methods research on a specific topic | Synthesize findings of methods qualitatively | Synthesize findings of methods research quantitatively |
| Included publications/ unit of analysis | Individual applied studies  | Individual applied studies  | Methods research papers | Methods research papers | Methods research papers |
| Sampling strategy | Random, purposeful, stratified, matched, complete^a^  | Stratified, matched, complete^a^ | Complete^a^   | Complete^a^,  purposeful | Complete^a^ |
| Typical analytic approach | Qualitative categorisation and descriptive statistics | Meta-regression | Qualitative categorisation and descriptive statistics | Qualitative synthesis | Meta-analysis |
| Role of quality assessment  | Often as an outcome  | Possible as an exposure or covariable | Usually not performed | Step in synthesis process^b^ | Step in synthesis process^b^ |
| Analogy in health research | Observational study (prevalence) | Observational study (exposure-outcome) | Scoping review | Qualitative evidence synthesis | Quantitative evidence synthesis|
:::{.small}
^a^Usually based on a comprehensive search process that aims to find all eligible publications as completely as possible.
^b^Quality criteria currently remain unclear for most types of methods research.
:::
:::
